content: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition in children, characterized by symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. There has been growing interest in exploring complementary and alternative therapies, such as acupuncture, for managing ADHD. However, the current body of evidence does not clearly establish whether acupuncture is an effective treatment for children and adolescents with ADHD. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture as a therapeutic intervention for ADHD in individuals under the age of 18. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including CENTRAL, MEDLINE, CINAHL, EMBASE, ERIC, PsycINFO, and several Chinese databases, up to May 2010. Additionally, Chinese-language journals and conference proceedings were manually searched to ensure thorough coverage of the available literature. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-randomized controlled trials that compared acupuncture with placebo, sham acupuncture, or conventional treatments. Participants were required to be under 18 years of age and diagnosed with any type of ADHD. Studies published in any language were considered eligible for inclusion. Two independent reviewers assessed the studies for inclusion based on predefined criteria and extracted data using standardized forms. The risk of bias in the included trials was evaluated with respect to allocation concealment, blinding, and participant withdrawals. ADHD outcomes were measured using core symptom rating scales, and additional secondary outcomes were also considered. Despite the extensive search, no studies met the inclusion criteria for this review. As a result, there is no evidence from randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials to support the use of acupuncture as a treatment for ADHD in children and adolescents. Consequently, no conclusions can be drawn regarding the efficacy or safety of acupuncture for this population. This review underscores the need for further research in this area. High-quality, large-scale randomized controlled trials are essential to determine whether acupuncture is a viable treatment option for ADHD in children and adolescents.
